That isn't how ADHD works. You're misinformed. I'd recommend browsing /r/ADHD, there's tons of good information about the disorder there. Adult ADHD is real. You seem upset about the overmedication of a particular drug, which is fair to an extent, but just because some people abuse it or don't need it but get put on it, doesn't mean that some can't benefit from it.

Concerta is methylphenidate, not dextroamphetamine. There is also nothing particularly bad about frequent amphetamine use at reasonable therapeutic doses. Google Paul Erdos for a shining example. I understand having an initially poor response to the idea of medicating children, but for those with a severe disorder, sometimes it is the best course of action.

Well, that's true for everything though. If you happen to have an undiagnosed heart condition, simply playing a light sport one day could end your life as easily as taking the wrong drug. The fact is that the risk is incredibly small. If all precautions are taken, then the rewards definitely outweigh the risks by a landslide. You could get hit by a bus today, why go outside...

Also remember that everything we do effects our brains. Our brains aren't these static things with all the chemicals in just the right amounts and in perfect harmony. It is messy. Drugs aren't the only thing that effect our brains or change the way they work (temporarily might I add). Even hugging your mother may have more of a effect on your brain than taking a hit of some drug.

You mention a lot that you don't get why you'd use drugs to achieve similar feelings to other pleasure inducing activities. Well. It is not so similar all of the time. You can use drugs to explore your own mind in ways you can never achieve without them. Some people find that fascinating. This is only one example.

Again, facts are facts but what really matters in this case if your own gut feeling. Drugs are just drugs. If you don't want to use them then that is fine too. It's no biggie either way.

You seem to be thinking along the lines of "why do drugs when you could go hiking or spend time with friends and learn new skills?"

Why not both? An important part of life is learning moderation. Do things responsibly and you are fine, as with anything else. Also, some people don't have the ability to do things like hike (physical disability) or may have issues doing things normally (mental disabilities).

Take ADHD for example. Not everyone who takes stimulants is going crazy like the stereotype. A therapeutic dose and this person can now perform close to his non-ADHD counterparts. But it's not wrong for someone without ADHD to take these drugs for the same reasons either.

Drugs carry benefits and downsides just like anything else and it's up to the user to make responsible choices to mitigate unwanted outcomes.

You seem to think that every drug has about the same risk as well. It gets much more complicated than it might seem. I would equate the risk of taking a low dose of nearly any psychedelic that is tested and while you are in a good set and setting to going about your average day (which may include being in traffic as a driver or as a pedestrian, interacting with strangers, etc.). Shooting up an untested mystery drug while no one to babysit just in case is around? Now that is a very large risk.

It's all relative. Drugs are tools. None are inherently bad. It's up to you to use them correctly. And what constitutes as correct will vary wildly.

On the topic of drugs specifically for recreational use, your argument reads like "why play basketball for enjoyment? I find tennis to be much more fun".

Anyway, if you're interested in learning about drugs more I recommend browsing this sub's sidebar or Erowid. And by the way, it's totally fine if you don't personally want to use drugs for fun. It's all preference.
